title: On the 100% Rule of Linear Programming
summary: The so-called ``100% rule'' is a somewhat classical and yet somehow obscure rule that gives some local sensitivity-analysis information based on the very limited local sensitivity-analysis information that is often made available by linear-programming software, derived from an optimal basis that is hidden from the user. Introduced in a classic undergraduate textbook in 1977, half a century ago, it was only picked up on by researchers in a very limited way, and while it appears in some undergraduate textbooks, it tends not to appear in most modern graduate-level textbooks.
